# Story 02 — Domain models, Django admin, demo seed

## Prerequisites

- [Story 01 completed](01-story-01-foundation.md): seven registered but **model-free** Django apps
  under `backend/apps/`, env-driven settings, `/api/v1/health/`, pytest-django, and a working
  `docker compose up`.
- Docker is installed and the stack is verified. **`docker compose exec api pytest` is the canonical
  test command** — it runs against PostgreSQL. The host-side SQLite loop still works and stays green.
- **No migrations exist anywhere.** Confirm with
  `find backend/apps -path '*/migrations/*.py' -not -name '__init__.py'` returning nothing before you
  start. This story consumes a one-time window (see Backend Task 1).

---

## Story Goal

Define the entire data model in a single migration pass, register every model in Django admin, and
write a `seed_demo` command that fills the database with credible bilingual demo data.

Two things carry unusual weight.

**Django admin is this product's entire back-office.** The "Admin" item in the top navigation links
to `/admin/`, not to a React screen. Everything an administrator manages — users, roles, departments,
branches, categories, tags, SLA policies, canned replies, the audit log — is managed there and will
never be built in React. That is a deliberate trade that buys two to three stories of time, and it
only pays off if the admin is configured properly: `list_display`, `list_filter`, `search_fields`,
inlines, readonly system fields. Admin config here is a **feature**, not a debug aid.

**`seed_demo` is what makes every later story demonstrable.** A queue with four rows proves nothing.
The seed must produce enough variety that every UI state in `docs/design/` has real data behind it,
and enough history that story 09's 90-day report range shows a real curve.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Custom user model, and the one-time ordering constraint

**This must happen before any `makemigrations` runs.** `AUTH_USER_MODEL` cannot be changed after the
first migration without deleting and regenerating every migration file. Order strictly:

1. Write `apps/accounts/models.py` in full (below).
2. Add `AUTH_USER_MODEL = "accounts.User"` to `backend/config/settings.py`, **replacing** the
   placeholder comment at ~line 96.
3. Only then run `makemigrations` (Backend Task 6).

**File: `backend/apps/accounts/models.py`**

```python
from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser
from django.db import models


class Department(models.Model):
    """A support department. Tickets route to one; agents belong to one."""

    name_en = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    name_ar = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    code = models.SlugField(max_length=32, unique=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["code"]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.name_en


class Branch(models.Model):
    """A physical branch. Shown on the customer card in the agent workspace."""

    name_en = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    name_ar = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    code = models.SlugField(max_length=32, unique=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["code"]
        verbose_name_plural = "branches"

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.name_en


class User(AbstractUser):
    """Roles here are the equivalent of Odoo groups.

    Story 03 turns `role` into DRF permission classes plus get_queryset() scoping —
    the two layers Odoo splits between ir.model.access and record rules.
    """

    class Role(models.TextChoices):
        ADMIN = "admin", "Administrator"
        MANAGER = "manager", "Manager"
        AGENT = "agent", "Agent"
        CUSTOMER = "customer", "Customer"

    class Language(models.TextChoices):
        EN = "en", "English"
        AR = "ar", "العربية"

    role = models.CharField(
        max_length=16, choices=Role.choices, default=Role.AGENT, db_index=True
    )
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=32, blank=True)
    department = models.ForeignKey(
        Department, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="members"
    )
    branch = models.ForeignKey(
        Branch, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="staff"
    )
    tier = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(
        default=1, help_text="Support tier. The design shows 'Tier 2' on the user chip."
    )
    language = models.CharField(max_length=2, choices=Language.choices, default=Language.EN)
    is_available = models.BooleanField(
        default=True, help_text="Round-robin assignment in story 05 skips unavailable agents."
    )
    # String reference: customers.Customer also points back at User, so the two apps
    # are mutually dependent. Django resolves the migration order itself.
    customer = models.ForeignKey(
        "customers.Customer",
        null=True,
        blank=True,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        related_name="portal_users",
        help_text="Set only for role=customer — links a portal login to its Customer record.",
    )

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.get_full_name() or self.username


class AuditLog(models.Model):
    """Append-only. Story 03 writes these from post_save/post_delete signals."""

    actor = models.ForeignKey(
        settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL,
        null=True,
        blank=True,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        related_name="audit_entries",
    )
    action = models.CharField(max_length=24, db_index=True)
    model_name = models.CharField(max_length=64, db_index=True)
    object_id = models.CharField(max_length=64, db_index=True)
    changes = models.JSONField(default=dict, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["-created_at"]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.action} {self.model_name}#{self.object_id}"
```

### 4 — Ticket, and how `number` is generated

**Read this section before writing it.** The intake suggests *"`select_for_update` or a DB sequence"*.
Neither is used, for three concrete reasons:

- A counter row to lock would require an **eighteenth model**, and the intake says *"exactly these
  models, no more"*.
- Locking the last `Ticket` row instead is gap-prone: under READ COMMITTED two transactions can
  disagree about which row is "last" around an in-flight insert.
- A Postgres sequence breaks the SQLite fallback that story 01 built and verified.

What is used instead: **`unique=True` on `number`, plus a bounded retry on `IntegrityError`.** The
unique constraint is what actually guarantees "never reused" — the database enforces it regardless of
isolation level or engine. The loop only handles the collision. Put the reasoning in a comment so it
does not read as having overlooked the intake.

```python
NUMBER_PREFIX = "TK-"
NUMBER_WIDTH = 4
MAX_NUMBER_ATTEMPTS = 10


class Ticket(models.Model):
    number = models.CharField(max_length=16, unique=True, editable=False, db_index=True)
    subject = models.CharField(max_length=240)
    description = models.TextField(blank=True)

    customer = models.ForeignKey("customers.Customer", on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="tickets")
    contact = models.ForeignKey("customers.Contact", null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="tickets")
    category = models.ForeignKey(Category, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="tickets")
    tags = models.ManyToManyField(Tag, blank=True, related_name="tickets")

    priority = models.CharField(max_length=8, choices=Priority.choices, default=Priority.NORMAL, db_index=True)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=12, choices=Status.choices, default=Status.NEW, db_index=True)
    channel = models.CharField(max_length=10, choices=Channel.choices, default=Channel.WEB, db_index=True)

    assignee = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="assigned_tickets")
    watchers = models.ManyToManyField(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, blank=True, related_name="watched_tickets")
    department = models.ForeignKey("accounts.Department", null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="tickets")
    branch = models.ForeignKey("accounts.Branch", null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="tickets")

    # Human-readable provenance. The design renders this verbatim:
    # "Owner · auto-assigned by rule R-12". Story 05's round-robin writes it.
    assignment_reason = models.CharField(max_length=160, blank=True)
    escalation_level = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(default=0)
    escalated_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)

    created_by = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="tickets_created")
    first_response_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    resolved_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    closed_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)

    # Written by story 05's sla_service. Stored, never computed here.
    sla_policy = models.ForeignKey(SLAPolicy, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="tickets")
    sla_response_due_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    sla_resolution_due_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    sla_response_breached = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    sla_resolution_breached = models.BooleanField(default=False)

    # Advisory only. Story 05's AI endpoints write these; nothing else reads them
    # to make a decision. The agent always approves.
    ai_summary = models.TextField(blank=True)
    ai_suggested_category = models.ForeignKey(Category, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="ai_suggested_for")

    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["-created_at"]
        indexes = [
            models.Index(fields=["status", "priority"]),
            models.Index(fields=["assignee", "status"]),
        ]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.number} — {self.subject}"
```

**Number generation** — a module-level helper plus a `save()` override:

```python
def next_ticket_number() -> str:
    last = Ticket.objects.order_by("-id").values_list("number", flat=True).first()
    seq = int(last.removeprefix(NUMBER_PREFIX)) + 1 if last else 1
    return f"{NUMBER_PREFIX}{seq:0{NUMBER_WIDTH}d}"
```

In `Ticket.save()`: return `super().save()` immediately when `self.number` is already set. Otherwise
loop up to `MAX_NUMBER_ATTEMPTS`: assign `next_ticket_number()`, `super().save()` inside
`transaction.atomic()`, and on `IntegrityError` **re-raise unless a Ticket with that exact number now
exists** — only a genuine number collision is retryable; any other constraint failure must surface.
Exhausting the attempts re-raises.

Two remaining models in the same file:

`TicketMessage` — `ticket` (FK, `CASCADE`, `related_name="messages"`), `author` (FK user, `SET_NULL`,
null), `body` (TextField), `is_internal` (Boolean default False, `db_index=True`), `channel` (Channel
choices), `created_at` (`auto_now_add`). `Meta.ordering = ["created_at"]`.
**`is_internal` is a trust boundary** — story 05's portal serializers filter on it, so it is indexed
and never nullable.

`TicketEvent` — `ticket` (FK, `CASCADE`, `related_name="events"`), `actor` (FK user, `SET_NULL`,
null), `event_type` (CharField 32, `db_index=True`), `field` (CharField 64, blank),

`Attachment` — `ticket` (FK, `CASCADE`, `related_name="attachments"`), `message` (FK

### 6 — Migrations

Run **once**, after every `models.py` above is complete and `AUTH_USER_MODEL` is set:

```bash
docker compose exec api python manage.py makemigrations accounts customers tickets kb
docker compose exec api python manage.py migrate
```

Expect `0001_initial` in each of the four apps and nothing in `ai`, `reports` or `portal` — those
three hold no models by design. Django emits `migrations.swappable_dependency(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL)`
for the circular `User ↔ Customer` reference; **do not hand-edit it**.

### 7 — Django admin — the back-office

Register every model. This is a feature, not scaffolding. Per model set `list_display`,
`list_filter`, `search_fields`, and `ordering`. Specifics that matter:

**File: `backend/apps/tickets/admin.py`**

- `TicketAdmin`: `list_display = ("number", "subject", "customer", "status", "priority", "channel", "assignee", "sla_resolution_due_at", "created_at")`;
  `list_filter = ("status", "priority", "channel", "department", "branch", "category")`;
  `search_fields = ("number", "subject", "customer__name", "customer__company")`;
  `readonly_fields = ("number", "created_at", "updated_at", "first_response_at", "resolved_at", "closed_at", "sla_response_due_at", "sla_resolution_due_at")`;
  `inlines = [TicketMessageInline, AttachmentInline]`;
  `filter_horizontal = ("tags", "watchers")`;
  **`list_select_related = ("customer", "assignee", "category", "department")`** and
  `def get_queryset(...)` adding `.prefetch_related("tags")`.
- `TicketEventInline` is **not** added — the activity log is append-only and long; expose it as its

- `AuditLogAdmin`: all fields readonly, `has_add_permission` and `has_change_permission` return

**File: `backend/apps/accounts/admin.py`** — extend `django.contrib.auth.admin.UserAdmin` rather than
registering a bare `ModelAdmin`, so the password field keeps its hashing widget. Add the custom

### 8 — `seed_demo`

**Create file: `backend/apps/tickets/management/commands/seed_demo.py`**
(plus empty `__init__.py` in `management/` and `management/commands/`).

Volume: **~150 tickets spread across the last 90 days**, so story 09's 7/30/90-day range selector and
its agent-performance table show real curves rather than a flat line.

**The requirement most likely to be missed: every timestamp is relative to `timezone.now()` at run
time, never hard-coded.** A seed written with fixed dates shows every ticket breached the day after
it was run, and the demo rots silently. Derive `created_at` as `now - timedelta(days=random_days)`
and the SLA due timestamps from that, re-computed on every run.

Because timestamps move, **idempotency means stable identities, not stable rows**: key every
`get_or_create` on a natural key (`Department.code`, `Customer.email`, `Ticket.number`,
`KBArticle.slug`, `CannedReply.shortcut`, `User.username`). Running the command twice must leave
object counts unchanged. Use `random.Random(20260826)` — a seeded instance, not the global module —
so choices are reproducible while timestamps stay live.

`created_at` is `auto_now_add`, so it cannot be set on create. Write the row, then
`Ticket.objects.filter(pk=...).update(created_at=...)` to backdate it — `update()` bypasses
`auto_now_add`. Same for `TicketMessage.created_at`.

Must produce:

- **4 logins**, one per role: `admin@demo`, `manager@demo`, `agent@demo`, `customer@demo`, plus 4–5
  extra agents so the agent-performance table has rows. One shared password, printed in a summary
  block at the end and documented in the README. `customer@demo` has `role=customer` and its
  `customer` FK set.
- **3 departments** (Billing, Technical, General) and **3 branches** (Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam), with
  genuine Arabic names.
- **≥ 8 customers** spanning all three tiers, each with 1–3 contacts (one `is_primary`) and 1–2 notes.
- **4 SLA policies** keyed to `(customer_tier, priority)` — at minimum Enterprise-P1 (30 min / 8 h),
  Premium-P1, Enterprise-Normal, Standard-Normal. Names match the design's "Enterprise-P1".
- **~150 tickets** covering **all 5 channels, all 8 statuses, all 4 priorities**, with an explicit
  SLA spread computed against `now`: most comfortable, **≥ 3 within 10 % of breach**, **≥ 3 already
  breached**, **≥ 2 escalated** (`status=escalated`, `escalation_level ≥ 1`, `escalated_at` set).
  Roughly a third assigned with a realistic `assignment_reason`; the rest unassigned so story 07's
  *Unassigned* tab is populated.
- **Conversation threads** — 1–6 `TicketMessage` rows per ticket mixing public replies and internal
  notes, and a `TicketEvent` trail (`created`, `assigned`, `status_changed`, `message_added`) so the
  Activity log tab is not empty.
- **CSAT** on ~60 % of resolved/closed tickets, skewed positive (mostly 4–5) so the story 09
  distribution chart is believable.
- **≥ 8 KB articles** across **≥ 3 categories**, each with **genuine Arabic and English text** — real
  sentences a native reader would accept, not lorem ipsum and not machine-mangled. Leave **one
  article with `body_ar` empty on purpose** so story 08's completeness indicator has a case to show.
  Topics should match the design: delayed SMS notifications, Arabic invoice templates, adding a
  branch, exporting the audit log, understanding a monthly statement.
- **≥ 6 canned replies** matching the design's chips: "Acknowledge + ETA", "Request invoice number",
  "Payment link sent", "Escalating to billing", "Ask to confirm resolved".

`--flush` deletes seeded data first, in FK-safe order (tickets before customers before users), then
re-seeds. Guard it with a refusal when `DEBUG` is False.

Finish with a summary table of created counts and the demo credentials.

### 9 — Tests

**Create file: `backend/apps/tickets/tests/test_numbering.py`** (with `__init__.py`):

- Sequential creates produce `TK-0001`, `TK-0002`, `TK-0003`.
- An explicitly supplied `number` is preserved, not overwritten.
- **Concurrency:** 50 tickets created from a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, asserting 50 distinct numbers and
  no `IntegrityError`. Mark it `@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)` and guard it:

  ```python
  pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
      connection.vendor != "postgresql",
      reason="SQLite serialises writes and raises 'database is locked' under threads; "
             "the real race is only exercised against PostgreSQL "
             "(docker compose exec api pytest).",
  )
  ```

  A skip with a stated reason is honest; a green test on SQLite that never raced would not be.

**Create file: `backend/apps/tickets/tests/test_seed_demo.py`**:

- `call_command("seed_demo")` twice leaves identical counts for `User`, `Customer`, `Ticket`,
  `KBArticle` — the idempotency assertion.
- After one run: all 5 channels, all 8 statuses and all 4 priorities are present; at least 3 tickets
  have `sla_resolution_due_at < now`; at least 2 have `status="escalated"`.
- At least one `KBArticle` has non-empty `body_ar`, and at least one has it empty.

**Create file: `backend/tests/test_admin_smoke.py`**: log in a superuser and `GET` the changelist for
**every** registered model via `django.contrib.admin.site._registry`, asserting HTTP 200. One loop
covers all seventeen and catches a bad `list_display` or `list_filter` immediately.

## Verification Steps

1. **Migrations are complete and consistent:**
   `docker compose exec api python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` — exits 0 with
   "No changes detected". A non-zero exit means a model change was never migrated.
2. **Clean migrate from empty:** `docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d && docker compose exec api python manage.py migrate` —
   no errors, including the swappable-dependency ordering for `User ↔ Customer`.
3. **Seed runs and is idempotent:**
   `docker compose exec api python manage.py seed_demo` then run it again. Object counts identical
   the second time; credentials printed both times.
4. **Admin is usable:** log in at `http://localhost:8000/admin/` as `admin@demo` and open the Tickets
   changelist. Confirm ~150 rows, working filters for status/priority/channel, search by ticket
   number and customer name, and the message/attachment inlines on a ticket detail page.
5. **No N+1 on the admin list:** with Tickets open, `docker compose logs api | tail -50` should show
   a bounded query count, not one per row. `list_select_related` is doing its job.
6. **Tests:** `docker compose exec api pytest -q` — all green, including the 50-thread concurrency
   test (Postgres). Then `cd backend && pytest -q` on the host — green, with the concurrency test
   **skipped and the reason printed**.
7. **Regression:** `curl -s localhost:8000/api/v1/health/` still returns
   `{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}`, and `/api/v1/docs/` still renders.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `AUTH_USER_MODEL = "accounts.User"` set **before** the first migration; the placeholder comment
      in `settings.py` is replaced.
- [ ] All seventeen models from the intake exist — and **no others**.
- [ ] `makemigrations` then `migrate` runs clean against an empty PostgreSQL database, and
      `makemigrations --check --dry-run` reports no pending changes.
- [ ] `Ticket.number` is generated as `TK-0001`, `TK-0002`, … is `unique=True`, and is never reused.
      The generation strategy is explained in a code comment.
- [ ] Every model is registered in Django admin with `list_display`, `list_filter` and
      `search_fields`; `Ticket` has message and attachment inlines; system fields are readonly;
      `AuditLog` cannot be added or edited.
- [ ] Admin changelists use `list_select_related` / `prefetch_related` — no per-row queries.
- [ ] `seed_demo` creates 4 role logins plus extra agents, ≥ 8 customers across all three tiers,
      ~150 tickets over 90 days covering all 5 channels / 8 statuses / 4 priorities, with ≥ 3 near
      breach, ≥ 3 breached and ≥ 2 escalated **computed relative to run time**.
- [ ] ≥ 8 KB articles with genuine Arabic and English, one deliberately missing `body_ar`;
      ≥ 6 canned replies; 4 SLA policies.
- [ ] `seed_demo` is idempotent; `seed_demo --flush` clears and re-seeds.
- [ ] Tests green: numbering sequential and unique under 50 concurrent creates on Postgres (skipped
      with a reason on SQLite), seed idempotency, and an admin changelist smoke test over every
      registered model.
- [ ] README documents the demo logins and the `docker compose exec api pytest` command.
- [ ] **Entry appended to `docs/AI_USAGE.md`** using the template in `docs/00-project-brief.md`
      section 5, with elapsed time recorded.
- [ ] `.squad/plans/crm-mvp/00-overview.md` updated with this story.
